answer: No, you should not still be taking lisinopril. Your records show that Dr. Marsh stopped lisinopril 10 mg on September 22, 2025, because of a dry cough, and started losartan 50 mg once daily in its place. Your later records agree: the December 2025 visit noted the cough had resolved, the March 2026 hospital discharge said to continue losartan, and the June 15, 2026 visit said to continue your current medicines. None of them restart lisinopril. The app that still lists it is most likely showing an old entry from a March 2025 record download, which was made before the change. Please don't take lisinopril. Ask your pharmacy or Dr. Marsh's office to remove it from the app and your medication list. Your records also list lisinopril as an intolerance because of the cough, so tell any doctor or pharmacist who prescribes for you about that.
short: Lisinopril 10 mg was stopped on September 22, 2025 for dry cough and replaced by losartan 50 mg daily. A later listing in an old app is out of date; please have it removed.

knowledge.says: A dry cough is a known side effect of ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril. It usually goes away after stopping the drug, which is why it is often recorded as an intolerance.
